claim: Concurrent verbal working memory task can eliminate the color-word Stroop effect.
source: Concurrent verbal working memory task can eliminate the color-word Stroop effect.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research (Kim et al., 2005; Luna et al., 2020; Park et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2014) as mentioned in the Introduction.

claim: The Stroop effect is characterized by lower accuracy and/or longer reaction times in incongruent trials compared to congruent trials.
source: One of the most commonly employed experimental paradigms for evaluating conflict processing is the color-word Stroop task, which is characterized by lower accuracy and/or longer reaction times (RTs) in incongruent trials compared to congruent trials (Stroop, 1935).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stroop (1935) and represents established knowledge about the Stroop task.

claim: When substantial resources are allocated to maintaining memory information, the resources required to process same-dimension distractors are occupied, reducing the interference caused by the distractors.
source: When substantial resources are allocated to maintaining memory information, the resources required to process same-dimension distractors are occupied, reducing the interference caused by the distractors (Brockhoff et al., 2022; Luna et al., 2020; Park et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Brockhoff et al., 2022; Luna et al., 2020; Park et al., 2007).

claim: Stroop conflict processing comprises multiple successive subprocesses, including stimulus processing, stimulus-response mapping, and response output stage.
source: Stroop conflict processing should be understood not as a single process but as multiple successive subprocesses, including stimulus processing, stimulus-response mapping, and response output stage (Banich, 2019; Parris et al., 2022; Viviani et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations to recent research (Banich, 2019; Parris et al., 2022; Viviani et al., 2024).

claim: The sensory cortex is crucial for maintaining visual content by modulating sensory gain, thereby biasing processing toward relevant stimuli.
source: The sensory recruitment hypothesis posits that the sensory cortex is crucial for maintaining visual content by modulating sensory gain, thereby biasing processing toward relevant stimuli (Hallenbeck et al., 2021; Wolff et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hallenbeck et al., 2021 and Wolff et al., 2020.

claim: The Stroop conflict relies more on the input-driven allocation of attention to perceptual features.
source: Moreover, several researchers have suggested that the Stroop conflict relies more on the input-driven allocation of attention to perceptual features (Algom et al., 2022; Bugg and Crump, 2012; Haciahmet et al., 2023; Schmidt, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Algom et al., 2022; Bugg and Crump, 2012; Haciahmet et al., 2023; Schmidt, 2019).

claim: The working memory system comprises not only sensory buffers but also a central system that mainly recruits the prefrontal cortex.
source: The theoretical underpinning is that the working memory system comprises not only sensory buffers but also a central system (Baddeley, 2012) that mainly recruits the prefrontal cortex, partially overlapping with the brain networks involved in Stroop conflict processing (Friehs et al., 2020; Okayasu et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baddeley, 2012; Friehs et al., 2020; Okayasu et al., 2023.

claim: Filtering out highly familiar and easily processed semantic information during the early sensory processing stage is difficult for individuals.
source: Furthermore, some research indicated that filtering out highly familiar and easily processed semantic information during the early sensory processing stage is difficult for individuals (Augustinova et al., 2019; Cavanagh and Frank, 2014; Itthipuripat et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Augustinova et al., 2019; Cavanagh and Frank, 2014; Itthipuripat et al., 2019.

claim: Occipito-parietal P1 signifies the earliest stage of top-down processes in early sensory processing, gating the direction of information processing in the brain.
source: Previous studies have proposed that within cognitive control mechanisms, occipito-parietal P1 signifies the earliest stage of top-down processes in early sensory processing, gating the direction of information processing in the brain (Klimesch et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Klimesch et al., 2007.

claim: N450 is a central-parietal negative deflection that exhibits greater negativity in incongruent trials compared to congruent trials within 350–500 ms after stimulus onsets.
source: N450 is a central-parietal negative deflection that exhibits greater negativity in incongruent trials compared to congruent trials within 350–500 ms after stimulus onsets, which is typically interpreted as conflict monitoring, the process of evaluating conflict levels and communicating the conflict information to control systems (Coderre et al., 2011; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations to Coderre et al., 2011; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2024.

claim: N450 is typically interpreted as conflict monitoring, the process of evaluating conflict levels and communicating the conflict information to control systems.
source: N450 is a central-parietal negative deflection that exhibits greater negativity in incongruent trials compared to congruent trials within 350–500 ms after stimulus onsets, which is typically interpreted as conflict monitoring, the process of evaluating conflict levels and communicating the conflict information to control systems (Coderre et al., 2011; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations to Coderre et al., 2011; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2024.

claim: The SP component shows a centro-parietal positive deflection from approximately 600 to 1000 ms in incongruent conditions.
source: As for the SP component, it shows a centro-parietal positive deflection from approximately 600 to 1000 ms in incongruent conditions, which is regarded as an index of conflict resolution (Di Russo and Bianco, 2023; Donohue et al., 2016; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Vo et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Di Russo and Bianco, 2023; Donohue et al., 2016; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Vo et al., 2021.

claim: The SP component is regarded as an index of conflict resolution.
source: As for the SP component, it shows a centro-parietal positive deflection from approximately 600 to 1000 ms in incongruent conditions, which is regarded as an index of conflict resolution (Di Russo and Bianco, 2023; Donohue et al., 2016; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Vo et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Di Russo and Bianco, 2023; Donohue et al., 2016; Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Vo et al., 2021.

claim: Fronto-central theta (4–7 Hz) power increases in conflict situations.
source: First, extensive research has found that fronto-central theta (4–7 Hz) power increases in conflict situations with the time windows of early and late theta band effects in stimulus-locked analyses corresponding to those of the N450 and SP effects, which suggests that early and late theta power reflects conflict detection and resolution processes, respectively (Yaar-Soffer et al., 2024; Senoussi et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yaar-Soffer et al., 2024; Senoussi et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Early and late theta power reflects conflict detection and resolution processes, respectively.
source: First, extensive research has found that fronto-central theta (4–7 Hz) power increases in conflict situations with the time windows of early and late theta band effects in stimulus-locked analyses corresponding to those of the N450 and SP effects, which suggests that early and late theta power reflects conflict detection and resolution processes, respectively (Yaar-Soffer et al., 2024; Senoussi et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yaar-Soffer et al., 2024; Senoussi et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Occipital-parietal alpha oscillations (8–13 Hz) can serve as a neural inverse index of mental activity or alertness, associated with the attentional engagement with visual stimuli during conflict processing.
source: Second, the occipital-parietal alpha oscillations (8–13 Hz) can serve as a neural inverse index of mental activity or alertness, associated with the attentional engagement with visual stimuli during conflict processing.
evidence: Supported by citations to Arakaki et al., 2022; Tafuro et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2023; Zhu et al., 2023 in the following sentence.

claim: Decreased alpha activity in the incongruent condition indicates enhanced attentional suppression.
source: The decreased alpha activity in the incongruent condition indicates enhanced attentional suppression (Arakaki et al., 2022; Tafuro et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2023; Zhu et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Arakaki et al., 2022; Tafuro et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2023; Zhu et al., 2023.

claim: The response incongruent trial evokes a smaller central beta power than the stimulus incongruent trial in the Stroop task.
source: Third, previous study has shown that the response incongruent trial evokes a small central beta power than the stimulus incongruent trial in the Stroop task (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: The suppressed effect of the central beta power most likely reflects the inhibition of proponent responses, associated with motion preparation.
source: The suppressed effect of the central beta power most likely reflects the inhibition of proponent responses, associated with motion preparation (Böttcher et al., 2023; Chung et al., 2024; Wendiggensen et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Böttcher et al., 2023; Chung et al., 2024; Wendiggensen et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: MVPA provides novel insight into the differences between two conditions by identifying the features that contribute most to classification.
source: As a data-driven technique, MVPA provides novel insight into the differences between two conditions by identifying the features that contribute most to classification (Li et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2023; Meier et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Li et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2023; Meier et al., 2012.

claim: RSA is a reliable way to uncover the neural mechanisms behind conflict processing.
source: Recent studies have suggested that RSA is a reliable way to uncover the neural mechanisms behind conflict processing (Freund et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2023), which helps identify which neural activities are central to the influence of working memory on Stroop conflict processing.
evidence: Supported by citations to Freund et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2023.

claim: The RTs of the single-task condition were faster than the dual-task condition.
source: The results showed that the RTs of the single-task condition were faster than the dual-task condition (main effect of task type: F(1, 31)=113.28, p<0.001, η2p=0.79)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data showing main effect of task type.

claim: There was a reliable Stroop interference effect across conditions.
source: and a reliable Stroop interference effect (main effect of congruency: F(1, 31)=32.53, p<0.001, η2p=0.51).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data showing main effect of congruency.

claim: The interaction between task type and congruency was significant for reaction times.
source: Notably, the interaction between task type and congruency was significant (F(1, 31)=8.62, p=0.006, η2p=0.22).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data showing significant interaction effect.

claim: In the single-task condition, the RTs of incongruent trials were significantly slower than congruent trials.
source: Simple effect analysis revealed that, in the single-task condition, the RTs of incongruent trials were significantly slower (M=851.15, SE = 32.16) than congruent trials (M=736.10, SE = 26.29) (p<0.001).
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of experimental data.

claim: In the dual-task condition, the RTs did not differ between incongruent trials and congruent trials.
source: However, in the dual-task condition, the RTs did not differ between incongruent trials (M=1073.04, SE = 39.73) and congruent trials (M=1033.68, SE = 49.43) (p=0.089)
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of experimental data.

claim: The Stroop effect of RTs only occurred in the single-task condition.
source: indicating that the Stroop effect of RTs only occurred in the single-task condition (Figure 1).
evidence: Supported by behavioral data analysis and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The P1 amplitude of the dual task was significantly greater than the single task.
source: Specifically, the P1 amplitude of the dual task (M=1.63, SE = 0.30) was significantly greater than the single task (M=0.39, SE = 0.28).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data showing main effect of task type on P1.

claim: For P1, neither the main effect of congruency nor the two-way interaction was significant.
source: However, neither the main effect of congruency (F(1, 31)=0.00, p=0.99, η2p=0.00) nor the two-way interaction (F(1, 31)=0.23, p=0.63, η2p=0.007) was significant (Figure 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data and shown in Figure 2.

claim: For N450, the main effect of task type and the main effect of congruency were both significant.
source: Analysis of the N450 component showed the main effect of task type (F(1, 31)=14.71, p=0.001, η2p=0.32) and the main effect of congruency (F(1, 31)=4.36, p<0.05, η2p=0.12) were both significant.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data.

claim: For N450, the two-way interaction was not significant.
source: However, the two-way interaction (F(1, 31)=0.63, p=0.43, η2p=0.02) was not significant (Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: For SP, the main effect of task type was significant.
source: For the SP component, two-way repeated-measures ANOVA showed the main effect of task type was significant (F(1, 31)=14.54, p=0.001, η2p=0.32)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data.

claim: For SP, the main effect of congruency was not significant.
source: but the main effect of congruency was not (F(1, 31)=2.89, p=0.10, η2p=0.09).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data.

claim: For SP, the interaction between congruency and task type was significant.
source: Importantly, the interaction between congruency and task type was significant (F(1, 31)=5.68, p<0.05, η2p=0.16).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of ERP data.

claim: In the single task, the SP amplitude in incongruent trials was significantly greater than in congruent trials.
source: Simple effect analysis showed that, in the single task, the SP amplitude in incongruent trials (M=1.29, SE = 0.39) was significantly greater than in congruent trials (M=0.70, SE = 0.30) (p=0.009).
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of ERP data.

claim: In the dual task, the SP amplitude did not differ between congruent trials and incongruent trials.
source: On the contrary, in the dual task, the SP amplitude did not differ between congruent trials (M=0.27, SE = 0.34) and incongruent trials (M=0.22, SE = 0.37) (p=0.98) (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of ERP data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Only one cluster in the theta band at 740–820 ms could significantly classify the Stroop effect of the single and dual tasks.
source: Cluster-level permutation tests of the theta band indicated that only one cluster in 740–820 ms could significantly classify the Stroop effect of the single and dual tasks (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by MVPA analysis results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The beta band showed a significant above-chance difference between the two task types from 920 to 1040 ms.
source: Regarding the beta band, tests showed a significant above-chance difference between the two task types from 920 to 1040 ms (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by MVPA analysis results and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: No reliable decoding was observed between the two task types in the alpha band.
source: However, no reliable decoding was observed between the two task types in the alpha band (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by MVPA analysis results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: For theta power, the main effect of congruency was significant.
source: The two-way repeated-measures ANOVA on theta power revealed that the main effect of congruency was significant (F(1, 31)=14.68, p=0.001, η2p=0.32)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: For theta power, the main effect of task type was not significant.
source: but the main effect of task type was not (F(1, 31)=0.30, p=0.59, η2p=0.01).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: For theta power, the interaction was significant.
source: Notably, the interaction was significant (F(1, 31)=7.71, p=0.009, η2p=0.20).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: In the dual task, the theta power did not differ between congruent trials and incongruent trials.
source: Simple effect analysis showed that, in the dual task, the theta power did not differ between congruent trials (M=3.12, SE = 0.24) and incongruent trials (M=3.27, SE = 0.24) (p=0.63).
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: In the single task, the theta power was significantly higher in incongruent trials than in congruent trials.
source: However, in the single task, the theta power was significantly higher in incongruent trials (M=4.00, SE = 0.32) than in congruent trials (M=2.68, SE = 0.20) (p<0.001) (Figure 6).
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of time-frequency data and shown in Figure 6.

claim: For beta power, the main effect of task type and the main effect of congruency were both significant.
source: Analysis of the beta power showed the main effect of task type (F(1, 31)=34.55, p<0.001, η2p=0.53) and the main effect of congruency (F(1, 31)=11.61, p=0.002, η2p=0.27) were both significant.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: For beta power, the interaction between task type and congruency reached a significant level.
source: Importantly, the interaction between task type and congruency reached a significant level (F(1, 31)=15.64, p<0.001, η2p=0.34).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: In the single-task condition, the beta power was significantly lower in the incongruent trials than in the congruent trials.
source: Simple effect analysis revealed that, in the single-task condition, the beta power was significantly lower in the incongruent trials (M=0.53, SE = 0.06) than in the congruent trials (M=0.80, SE = 0.08) (p<0.001)
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: In the dual-task condition, no significant difference in beta power was found between incongruent and congruent trials.
source: while no significant difference was found between them in the dual-task condition (p=0.40) (Figure 7).
evidence: Supported by simple effect analysis of time-frequency data and shown in Figure 7.

claim: The interaction pattern in the theta band significantly contributes to variation in the interaction pattern of response time.
source: The RSA results showed that the interaction pattern in the theta band significantly contributes to variation in the interaction pattern of response time (estimate = 0.17, SE = 0.05, t=3.22, pcorrected = 0.004).
evidence: Supported by RSA statistical analysis.

claim: The correlation between the dissimilarity matrix of the SP representation and the interaction pattern of response time was not significant.
source: However, the correlation between the dissimilarity matrix of the SP (estimate = 0.02, SE = 0.05, t=0.48, pcorrected = 0.63) and beta (estimate = 0.10, SE = 0.05, t=2.03, pcorrected = 0.06) representation and the interaction pattern of response time was not significant (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by RSA statistical analysis and shown in Figure 8.

claim: The correlation between the dissimilarity matrix of the beta representation and the interaction pattern of response time was not significant.
source: However, the correlation between the dissimilarity matrix of the SP (estimate = 0.02, SE = 0.05, t=0.48, pcorrected = 0.63) and beta (estimate = 0.10, SE = 0.05, t=2.03, pcorrected = 0.06) representation and the interaction pattern of response time was not significant (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by RSA statistical analysis and shown in Figure 8.

claim: For alpha power, the main effect of task type and the main effect of congruency were both significant.
source: Analysis of the alpha power showed the main effect of task type (F(1, 31)=57.90, p<0.001, η2p=0.65) and the main effect of congruency (F(1, 31)=7.38, p=0.01, η2p=0.19) were both significant.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data.

claim: For alpha power, the two-way interaction was not significant.
source: However, the two-way interaction (F(1, 31)=0.53, p=0.47, η2p=0.02) was not significant (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of time-frequency data and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: When the dimensions of memory information and distractors overlap, working memory processing modulates the late stage rather than the early stage of Stroop conflict processing.
source: All these results collectively suggested that, when the memorized information overlaps with the dimension of distractors, working memory processing modulates the late stage rather than the early stage of Stroop conflict processing.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined ERP, MVPA, and RSA results presented in the study.

claim: The Stroop interference effect was reduced under the dual-task condition, replicating previous findings.
source: Behaviorally, we found that the Stroop interference effect was reduced under the dual-task condition, replicating previous findings (Kim et al., 2005; Luna et al., 2020; Park et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citations to previous studies.

claim: Working memory load will occupy the limited resources necessary for distractor processing, diminishing the intensity of distractor processing and thereby reducing their interference with the task.
source: Working memory load will occupy the limited resources necessary for distractor processing, diminishing the intensity of distractor processing and thereby reducing their interference with the task.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on load theory (Murphy et al., 2016; Park et al., 2007) as cited in the text.

claim: Concurrent visual short-term working memory maintenance occupied the semantic resources required for distractor processing, resulting in the elimination of the Stroop effect.
source: In our study, concurrent visual short-term working memory maintenance occupied the semantic resources required for distractor processing, resulting in the elimination of the Stroop effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results and load theory.

claim: The processing of Chinese characters relies more on graphemic encoding and memory compared to English words.
source: However, in contrast to English words, the processing of Chinese characters relies more on graphemic encoding and memory (Chen, 1993).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen, 1993.

claim: Verbal working memory load can significantly modulate the Stroop effect.
source: Therefore, we believe that verbal working memory load can significantly modulate the Stroop effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results and comparison with previous studies.

claim: The working memory task influenced only the SP component, which reflects the process of conflict resolution.
source: The ERP findings indicated that the working memory task influenced only the SP component, which reflects the process of conflict resolution.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the ERP results presented.

claim: The SP amplitude is more positive in conflict situations.
source: Consistent with most research, our study showed that the SP amplitude is more positive in conflict situations (Heidlmayr et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citations to previous studies.

claim: Verbal working memory load eliminated the difference in SP between congruent and incongruent trials, indicating that conflict resolution did not occur in the dual-task condition.
source: Crucially, our study found that verbal working memory load eliminated the difference in SP between congruent and incongruent trials, indicating that conflict resolution did not occur in the dual-task condition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the SP results.

claim: Participants indeed detected the occurrence of conflict as indicated by the congruency effect at N450.
source: Additionally, our results revealed a congruency effect at N450, indicating that participants indeed detected the occurrence of conflict (Heidlmayr et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on the N450 results and citation to Heidlmayr et al., 2020.

claim: The early sensory input processing stage is insensitive to congruency effects.
source: Furthermore, our study did not find any differences in P1 between the different congruency conditions, which aligns with the findings of most studies that indicate the early sensory input processing stage is insensitive to congruency effects (David et al., 2011; Di Russo and Bianco, 2023).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citations to David et al., 2011; Di Russo and Bianco, 2023.

claim: Participants cannot suppress the processing of distractors at the perceptual level.
source: In other words, participants cannot suppress the processing of distractors at the perceptual level.
evidence: This is an inference based on the P1 results.

claim: Working memory influences the later stage of conflict resolution, while not influencing the early stage of perceptual processing and conflict detection.
source: Generally, the overall ERP results suggest that working memory influences the later stage of conflict resolution, while not influencing the early stage of perceptual processing and conflict detection.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the combined ERP results.

claim: Alpha is regarded as an indicator of top-down attentional modulation, with an increase in alpha reflecting the inhibition of distractor input.
source: Alpha is regarded as an indicator of top-down attentional modulation, with an increase in alpha reflecting the inhibition of distractor input (Van Diepen et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2023)
evidence: Supported by citations to Van Diepen et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2023.

claim: The patterns of attentional adjustment are similar across different task types in the study.
source: implying that the patterns of attentional adjustment are similar across different task types in our study (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the alpha band MVPA results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Late theta may represent the process of stimulus-response binding or mapping according to the framework of event coding theory.
source: According to the framework of event coding theory, late theta may represent the process of stimulus-response binding or mapping (Beste et al., 2023; Wendiggensen et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Beste et al., 2023; Wendiggensen et al., 2023.

claim: Theta is thought to be involved in adjusting the processing of stimulus information to correspond with appropriate responses.
source: For example, theta is thought to be involved in adjusting the processing of stimulus information to correspond with appropriate responses (Cavanagh et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cavanagh et al., 2009.

claim: About –200 to 0 ms before a response, higher theta activity is observed in high-conflict conditions compared to low-conflict conditions.
source: In line with this opinion, about –200 to 0 ms before a response, higher theta activity is observed in high-conflict conditions compared to low-conflict conditions (Cohen and Donner, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cohen and Donner, 2013.

claim: Working memory may eliminate the Stroop effect by influencing the stimulus-response mapping process.
source: Accordingly, working memory may eliminate the Stroop effect by influencing the stimulus-response mapping process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the theta band results and event coding theory.

claim: Beta activity is often thought to be associated with motor priming.
source: Beta activity is often thought to be associated with motor priming.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about beta activity.

claim: Beta decreases at the onset of movement.
source: Specifically, it decreases at the onset of movement (Jenkinson and Brown, 2011)
evidence: Supported by citation to Jenkinson and Brown, 2011.

claim: Beta increases during holding a static status.
source: but increases during holding a static status (Baker et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baker et al., 2001.

claim: Working memory may also influence the response output stage of Stroop conflict processing.
source: this result suggests that working memory may also influence the response output stage of Stroop conflict processing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the beta band results.

claim: The neural activity pattern of theta is most similar to the behavioral Stroop effect modulation pattern.
source: The RSA results further reveal that the neural activity pattern of theta is most similar to the behavioral Stroop effect modulation pattern.
evidence: This is a summary of the RSA results.

claim: A reduction in activation patterns reflects greater neural efficiency according to the standpoint of neural efficiency.
source: This result can be interpreted from the standpoint of neural efficiency, suggesting that a reduction in activation patterns reflects greater neural efficiency (Rypma et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rypma et al., 2006.

claim: The core reason for the disappearance of the behavioral Stroop effect under the dual-task condition is that, compared to congruent trials, neural activation in theta decreases and response speed increases in incongruent trials.
source: Therefore, we speculate that the core reason for the disappearance of the behavioral Stroop effect under the dual-task condition is that, compared to congruent trials, neural activation in theta decreases and response speed increases in incongruent trials (Figures 1 and 6C).
evidence: This is speculation based on the RSA results and neural efficiency principle, referencing Figures 1 and 6C.

claim: Theta can predict RTs according to many studies.
source: Moreover, this result aligns with many studies that have found theta can predict RTs (Kaiser and Schütz-Bosbach, 2021; Senoussi et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kaiser and Schütz-Bosbach, 2021; Senoussi et al., 2022.

claim: SP and beta may not be the core indicators directly determining the behavioral modulation effect.
source: However, although SP and beta exhibited interaction effects in the data patterns, they may not be the core indicators directly determining the behavioral modulation effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RSA results.

claim: SP, as an ERP component, contains multiple oscillatory bands, indicating several parallel brain processes.
source: SP, as an ERP component, contains multiple oscillatory bands, indicating several parallel brain processes (Yaar-Soffer et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yaar-Soffer et al., 2024.

claim: Theta oscillations are biological candidates for neuronal computation and communication, capable of integrating selection-related information during cognitive control to inform response execution.
source: Moreover, theta oscillations are biological candidates for neuronal computation and communication (Cavanagh and Frank, 2014), capable of integrating selection-related information during cognitive control to inform response execution (Duprez et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cavanagh and Frank, 2014; Duprez et al., 2020.

claim: Changes in beta bands may be influenced by theta bands.
source: Combined with the MVPA decoding results indicating that the beta band (920–1040 ms) follows the theta band (740–820 ms), we speculate that changes in beta bands may be influenced by theta bands.
evidence: This is speculation based on the temporal sequence of MVPA results.

claim: When the dimensions of working memory load overlap with those of distractor stimuli, individuals do not need to engage in conflict resolution.
source: Overall, when the dimensions of working memory load overlap with those of distractor stimuli, individuals do not need to engage in conflict resolution.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined results of the study.
